sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To make a noun plural, add *-k*. After a vowel that is all you add: *kávé* → *kávék*, *ajtó* → *ajtók*. After a consonant, a linking vowel goes in first, so the *-k* has something to sit on: *asztal* → *asztalok*, *szék* → *székek*. A final *-a* or *-e* also stretches to *-á* or *-é*: *lámpa* → *lámpák*. Which linking vowel? That follows vowel harmony, the pattern you already know from *asztalok* and *székek*.

English adds the same *-s* to everything. Hungarian cannot put *-k* straight after most consonants, so *könyvk* and *asztalk* are not words. Say the plural aloud with its linking vowel, *könyv-ek*, *asztal-ok*, until it sounds like one word.
